A free image compressor.
With room for your RAW photos.

Still helps photographers, creators, students and website owners make large photos easier to share. Use it as an online RAW image compressor for supported camera files, a HEIC to JPEG converter, or a simple way to reduce JPG, PNG and WebP file sizes. It is completely free for everyone, with no account or subscription required.

01 / ADD

Start with your originals.

Drop one photo or a batch of up to 30. Supported RAW and DNG files are developed into viewable images; HEIC, JPG, PNG and WebP photos work too.

02 / COMPRESS

Choose the size you need.

Compress images to a 2 MB, 3 MB or custom maximum. Choose WebP or JPEG and a longest edge, then let Still balance encoding quality and dimensions.

03 / SAVE

Check the detail. Download.

Compare the decoded original with the compressed photo, then download each export or a ZIP of the batch. Your original files stay untouched.

Image compression, explained.

Is Still completely free for everyone?

Yes. Still is completely free to use. There is no sign-up, subscription or payment required to compress and download photos. You can use it for personal photos, school projects or business websites. Browser limits still apply: up to 30 photos per batch and 200 MB per photo.

Can I use Still as a RAW image compressor for iPhone photos?

Yes, for supported RAW and DNG variants. Still develops the RAW photo and exports a smaller WebP or JPEG for your website; it does not produce a smaller editable RAW file. iPhone 12 Pro ProRAW DNG has been tested. Some newer JPEG XL-compressed ProRAW files may need a full-quality JPEG export from Apple Photos or Lightroom first. The app reports unsupported files rather than substituting a small thumbnail.

How do I compress an image to 2 MB or 3 MB?

Add your photos, select the 2 MB or 3 MB target, choose WebP or JPEG, and click Compress photos. The target is a maximum, so an export may be smaller. Still prioritizes high encoding quality and reduces dimensions when needed. If you select Original dimensions, it preserves the pixel dimensions and warns you when the output exceeds the target. A custom target can be set from 0.1 to 20 MB.

Can I compress RAW images without losing quality?

WebP and JPEG are lossy formats. They cannot retain all RAW editing data or HDR range. Still aims to preserve visible detail at a much smaller file size, and its before-and-after preview helps you inspect the result. Keep your original RAW files as master copies and inspect important downloads at full size.

Can I convert HEIC to JPEG or WebP for free?

Yes. Add your HEIC or HEIF photos, choose JPEG or WebP, and compress. This makes supported iPhone photos usable in websites and everyday photo workflows. Codec support depends on the file and browser; the app tells you if a photo cannot be read.

Are my photos uploaded to a server?

No. Image decoding, resizing, compression and ZIP creation happen on your device in the browser. Photo contents are not uploaded. The page loads its app files and sample image from GitHub Pages and its fonts from Google Fonts. Save your downloads before closing the tab, because exports are not stored in an account.
